rationale: Only setup is at risk: hold is +0.10 (repaired to margin at ff), DRV is 994 against a bar of 2881, and DRC is 0. The worst path (-0.962 at max_ss) is cone A, which is wire-heavy and was not touched by the resizer, so R1 leaves it only +0.028. The deciding evidence is that the post-CTS resizer (multi-corner, margin 0.247) upsized every and4 in two 21-stage chains (cones B and E), plus 5 gates in cone C, and added 5 rebuffers. All 50 _4 cells sit on nets with post-GRT slack <=0.2 and none are at 0.3-1.0. For these cones the post-GRT-to-signoff gap is 0.4-0.6 ns, more than the margin, so any repair that stops at the margin still fails signoff. At R1 the resizer needs about 1 ns less repair, and losing the upsizing (about 0.6-1.3 ns at ss) exceeds their R1 margins of 0.39, 0.61 and 0.41 ns. I expect WS(R1) of about -0.4, so C1 is about 16.97, and the step-back near 17.0 likely fails the same way.
